Internal: build the label / missing-value loss note for Excel and CSV saves

Source: R/io.R
dot-jst_jsave_label_loss_note.Rd

Excel and CSV cannot store variable labels, value labels, or missing-value declarations. jsave emits a note after a successful write to these formats describing what was (or, under preserve.declarations = FALSE, would have been) lost. The wording depends on which missing-value form the frame carried and on whether preserve.declarations = FALSE blanked the codes.

Usage

.jst_jsave_label_loss_note(
  ext,
  spss_vars,
  stata_vars,
  preserve.declarations,
  n_blanked,
  text_udm = FALSE,
  data = NULL,
  code_name = NULL,
  path = NULL
)

Arguments

ext

Lowercase target extension, "xlsx" or "csv".

spss_vars

Character vector of SPSS-form UDM variable names, as detected before any collapse.

stata_vars

Character vector of Stata-form tagged-NA variable names, as detected before any collapse.

preserve.declarations

Logical, the value passed to jsave.

n_blanked

Integer count of SPSS-style code cells blanked when preserve.declarations = FALSE; zero otherwise.

text_udm

Logical: is one of spss_vars a text variable? Its declared codes are words, so "ordinary numbers" becomes "ordinary values" (Session 351, the S340 item's rider).

data

The data frame as given, before any collapse: its labels and declarations.

code_name

Character; the data as the printed line names it (mydata for an expression, whose line the caller opens with "mydata <- ...").

path

Character; the path written, normalized.

Value

A single message string, or NULL if no note applies.

Details

Since Session 359 (the S357 item, Jeff's walk of missing_convention_walk.R Section 30) the note says only what the frame had to lose and names what the package knows:

  • The first line names labels only when a variable carries a variable label or value labels (the registration note's rule: it fires only on registrations), and missing-value metadata only when a variable declares missing values. A frame with neither gets no note.

  • SPSS-style codes write as literal numbers. The variables and the declared codes their cells hold are named – "Income's declared missing value -99 is written as an ordinary number and will read back as valid data." – where the note said "Any SPSS-style missing values (e.g. -99)". A declared code no cell holds writes nothing, and is not named.

  • The way to write them as empty cells is the jsave() call to run, with the data's name and the path just written, where the note gave "jsave(..., preserve.declarations = FALSE)", which does not run as printed (the S343 rule).

  • Stata-style missing values write as blank cells; the distinction between them is not preserved.

  • preserve.declarations = FALSE that blanked SPSS-style codes: a confirmation giving the count of blanked cells.

The note is a loss-of-fidelity warning per the locked jsave design; it is not gated to the joutput verbosity tiers.
